aria: Animated recap of the Wizards' 116 to 96 home win over the Magic: Bilal Coulibaly's 3-pointer late in the third quarter, Washington's 18th three, that made it 97 to 75, quarter-by-quarter scoring, Kyshawn George's 24 points with six threes, the top scorers, how the Wizards won, and the next game.

notes: Box score from the Wizards' 116–96 home win over the Orlando Magic on Nov 22, 2026, from the Covers box score; all 116 Washington points and all 96 Orlando points add up from the player lines, and the shooting totals (39 of 75, 22 of 39 from three, 16 of 20 FT for Washington; 36 of 88, 12 of 39, 12 of 13 for Orlando), rebounds (45–39), assists (31–27), steals (6–8), points in the paint (24–42), fast-break points (18–12) and Washington's biggest lead (25) are from Covers. The 22-of-39 three-point shooting is also in the AP and Field Level Media, and the Orlando Sentinel says the Magic trailed by as many as 25 and never led. The quarter scores (38–25–34–19 to 21–30–26–19) add up to both totals; the 38–21 first quarter, the 63–51 halftime score and the 97–77 score after three are also in Field Level Media (halftime also in the AP). Player lines used here also match the AP and Field Level Media (George 24 with 6 of 11 from three, Davis 22, Dybantsa 16 with 8 rebounds and 6 assists, Young 11 with 11 assists, Coulibaly 12, all on threes; da Silva 18, Bane 17, Wagner 16 with 8 rebounds and 6 assists). Records and ranks are from the site's standings after Sunday's games.

Washington's 22 threes were one short of the franchise record of 23, set in an overtime loss at Indiana on Feb. 12, 2025 (AP; Field Level Media); a would-be 23rd by Will Riley was ruled a two, his foot on the line (AP; Field Level Media). The Wizards opened the game on an 11–0 run and never trailed (AP), and have won three in a row for the first time since Feb. 1–5, 2025, after an early eight-game losing streak (AP). Orlando played without Paolo Banchero (sprained ankle, AP). Next: the Wizards host Boston on Tuesday, the Magic host Detroit on Tuesday (AP).

The play of the game is an original illustration of Bilal Coulibaly's three that made it 97–75: AP: "A 3 by Bilal Coulibaly made it 97-75 late in the third." Washington led 97–77 after three quarters (Field Level Media and the Covers line score), so it was the Wizards' last basket of the quarter, and with 18 threes through three quarters (Field Level Media; the Orlando Sentinel says that tied their season high) it was their 18th. The board's Wizards +19 to +22 is 94–75 to 97–75, which follows from the three. The exact clock isn't reported, so the scoreboard shows no time. The shot isn't described further, so it is drawn as the template's plain pull-up from beyond the arc. The figures are stylized and not traced from footage, and the spacing is not to scale.

The music is an original beat made for this page. No existing recordings or melodies are used. This is an unofficial fan recap, not affiliated with the Washington Wizards or the NBA, which is why it carries a plain basketball mark and the team's colors but not the team's logo.

The shooter in the play of the game is drawn to Coulibaly's listed 6-foot-7 and 195 pounds (Basketball-Reference, Wikipedia; RealGM lists 6-8), with arms at the default length because none of those sources reports a wingspan, in the Wizards' home kit with No. 0 (Wikipedia, Basketball-Reference) and the default darker skin tone, since he has no approved look yet. It is an original figure with a featureless face, not a portrait or a trace of footage.
